errors.quote:
episodic encoder queueing at 29\% mean
utilization, invisible to rate- and utilization-based monitors
errors.stated: the vision pool queues episodically at 29% mean utilization, with no configuration attached
errors.computed: The 29% is measured at one specific locked configuration -- the naive 2-encoder x 2-LLM topology at the trace's own recorded rate over the largest-burst window (twopool.tex:246-251, 337-341, 375). It is not a property of the deployed or SLA-shaped fleet: twopool.tex:344-347 says six encoder workers (3x this topology) are needed at the same rate, at which utilization would necessarily be lower still. Independent upper-bound check that the 29% is at least self-consistent: 83{,}376 forwards x 316.4 ms (the published per-forward maximum) / (2 workers x 8.3 h x 3600) = 44.1%, so 29% is admissible as a mean over sub-full batches; and 64{,}804 requests / (8.3 x 3600) = 2.169 req/s reproduces the quoted 2.2 req/s.
errors.relation: definitional scope of a headline utilization figure (which topology, which window)
errors.proposed_fix: Replace with: "episodic encoder queueing at 29\% mean utilization on the two-worker topology at the trace's own rate, invisible to rate- and utilization-based monitors".

notes:
SCOPE. tese.tex is the root/front-matter file: title page, Abstract, Resumo, draft note, abbreviations table, \include list, and a manual thebibliography. It contains no tables, no figures and no results sections, so there is no text-vs-table relation internal to this file. Every number in it is a restatement of a body-chapter result, which makes the only meaningful audit an abstract-vs-body recomputation; I therefore recomputed each of the nine distinct quantities against the chapter that produces it (trace-eda, twopool, baselines, predictors, closedloop, validation) rather than only checking abstract-vs-resumo.

EXTRACTOR FLAGS ADJUDICATED. (1) The claimed "deployable" vs "menor frota vi\'avel" denominator discrepancy is REFUTED as a numeric error -- baselines.tex:117-120 defines them to be the same fleet (C=8 = max over windows of C*) -- but I retain it at severity "ambiguous" because the abstract never defines "deployable" and the two language versions still read differently. (2) The extractor's demand that the two "order of magnitude" phrases be confirmed as >=10x and not ~6x is CONFIRMED: 11.97x (burstiness) and 10.7x (knees). (3) The verifiability gap the extractor raises for the four trace-EDA descriptors is real but out of scope for an internal-arithmetic pass; internally they are all mutually consistent, and the Jaccard one is fully reconstructible from the published set sizes.

OUT-OF-CHAPTER OBSERVATION worth routing to the twopool auditor: twopool.tex:79 states "TPOT 14.9 vs.\ 7.9~ms; 87 vs.\ 142 output tok/s per user". The identity tok/s = 1000/TPOT_ms gives 1000/14.9 = 67.1 and 1000/7.9 = 126.6, not 87 and 142, and the two discrepancy factors are not even equal (1.30x and 1.12x), so this is not a single consistent unit convention. It does not propagate into tese.tex, so I do not record it as a finding here, but it should be recomputed against the source data in the twopool pass.

SEVERITY CALIBRATION. Only one finding is arithmetic (the 0.96 -> 0.97 rounding), and it sits 0.0002 above the rounding boundary, so it is recorded as "rounding" not "wrong". The remaining six are scope, denominator-definition, cross-language-strength and document-structure defects; none of the thesis's headline numbers is numerically false.
